So apparently this was a big deal in the US. There were individual state laws in the early 1800's that defined who was black. For example Virgina (specifically Thomas Jefferson) had the understanding that a black person was at least 25% black. FL had a rule that you had to be >1/8 black. However these laws and definitions of race were used to discriminate against people in the Era of Jim Crow laws. There was also the "one drop rule" meaning that any drop of blood that wasn't white could define a persons race (Jewish, Black, Native American, ect). Think mugels in the Harry Potter world. Eventually this view fell out of favor and people were allowed to self identify on a new census (around the 1940's) that included 'multiracial' as an option and Jim Crow laws were outlawed. https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-drop_rule

Today the thought seems to be that if you can be seen as black, then you can identify as African American. Example controversies have been the white NAACP leader who self identified as black and heavily tanned to cover up her genetic whiteness. Also, there was a kid who was literally African American (South Africa) who was white and applied for an African American scholarship and was suspended for doing so. http://mobile.wnd.com/2004/01/22929/

Basically you have to have naturally dark skin. However, there is no legal definition other than you have to be able to trace yourself back to at least one black family member.
